records.name: Physicians for Social Responsibility Pennsylvania
records.summary: Doctors, nurses, and other health workers who speak up about pollution, climate, and energy in Pennsylvania. They hold public webinars and virtual meetings, run air monitoring and watchdog projects, and organize action campaigns.
records.what_you_do: Join a virtual meeting or public webinar, sign up for the newsletter and action alerts, or help with a project such as air monitoring or the concerned health professionals group.

schedule.text: Virtual meetings and webinars are listed on the events page with their dates, for example an October 21, 2026 virtual meeting. No regular weekly or monthly time is stated.

cost.text: Event costs are not stated. The group also takes donations and sustaining memberships, which are optional.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter, or pick a public event from the events page and register for it.
first_step.basis: Events and meetings are open to the public with a clear way to sign up.

records.notes: Lead from the Friends Center tenant directory (wave w13-congregations, agent r-quaker-meetings). The office is in Philadelphia, but the work is statewide and some events are held elsewhere (a November 3, 2026 event is in Pittsburgh). Blog posts show month and day only, so they were not used as dated evidence.

records.name: Junior Achievement of Southeastern Pennsylvania
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings lessons on money, work, and starting a business into schools and after-school programs. Volunteers from many kinds of jobs teach short classes and guide hands-on activities such as a budgeting simulation.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the volunteer form, choose a grade range and a schedule with a program manager, and attend a short training. Then share your work and life experience in classes, in person or virtually.

schedule.text: Classes run during the school year. The site lists a Fall 2026 JA Finance Park program and a 2026 to 2027 after-school company program. Class times are set between each volunteer and a program manager, and no fixed weekly time is given.

cost.text: No volunteer fee is listed. Participant costs are not stated on the pages read, and the group offers sponsorships.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer sign-up form, then attend the short training with a program manager.
first_step.basis: The sign-up steps are spelled out and a short training comes before teaching.

records.notes: Lead from the Friends Center tenant directory. The address on the site is for mail only, so no visiting address is recorded. The events page labels the Fall 2026 program as happening now but gives no month or dates, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The volunteer page lists a staff member's personal email for volunteer questions; it is left out here and the program phone line is recorded instead. Audience is set to public because volunteers are recruited from the public; the students served are reached through classes.

records.name: ACE Mentor Program of Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: A free after-school program that puts Philadelphia-area high school students on teams with architects, engineers, and construction professionals. Teams work on mock and real design challenges and attend career and professional development sessions.
records.what_you_do: Students apply online and return a parent consent form. Professionals can register as mentors, then complete a background check and training before joining a team.

schedule.text: Teams meet after school on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday at 4:00 pm. Students choose a fall semester, spring semester, or full-year team in the 2026 to 2027 program year.

locations.label: Office (teams meet at offices, schools, or job sites)

first_step.how: Complete the online registration form on the Students page, include a parent or guardian email for the consent form, and choose the Greater Philadelphia affiliate and your county.
first_step.basis: Any interested high school student can apply for free through a clear online form, though the sign-up has several steps.

records.notes: Resolved from the national ACE Mentor Program of America lead (acementor.org). The national finder page showed a Philadelphia national office address but no Philadelphia affiliate among its first 12 entries, and its pages 2 to 7 were not readable. One web search then found this Greater Philadelphia affiliate and its own site, so this record is the Philadelphia program a student can join. The national organization is not written as a separate record. Cost is from the affiliate's student page and a public third party page (phillygoes2college.org). Service area per the student page: Philadelphia, Montgomery, Chester and Delaware counties in Pennsylvania, and Camden and Cumberland counties in New Jersey. The location is the affiliate office; team meeting sites are not listed.

records.name: Philadelphia Youth Sports Collaborative
records.summary: A network of more than 170 youth sports programs across Philadelphia. It trains coaches and referees, shares safety guidance, and helps families find a sports program near home. It also works with the city on accessible recreation.
records.what_you_do: Families can use the Find A Provider list to locate a program. Coaches and referees can use the training and resources pages. Community groups can apply to become members and take part in trainings.

schedule.text: Events and trainings are posted on the events calendar with their own dates. Check the calendar for the current list.

cost.text: Youth sports provider fees vary by program. Costs for PYSC trainings and events are not stated on the pages read.

first_step.how: Use the Find A Provider link to find a youth sports program near you, or sign up for the email newsletter for trainings and events.
first_step.basis: Families can search the provider list directly, and public events and a newsletter sign-up are listed.

records.notes: Lead from the Friends Center tenant directory. Calendar dates have no year written, so they are not used as dated evidence. The most recent dated item with a year is a July 9, 2026 news post. Summary and locations describe the organization's own pages only.

records.name: Housing Alliance of Pennsylvania
records.summary: A statewide group that works for affordable housing and eviction prevention. It follows state lawmaking, posts legislative updates, supports housing workers with training, and invites members of the public to take action on housing policy.
records.what_you_do: Read the legislative updates, take action on housing bills, and sign up for the newsletter. Members get free educational webinars and a discount on the Homes Within Reach Conference, and volunteers can serve on committees and boards.

schedule.text: The Homes Within Reach Conference is set for December 14 to 16, 2026. Legislative updates and news posts come out about once a month. No regular meeting time is listed.

cost.text: Membership has an annual fee, but the amount is not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the newsletter, or ask staff by phone or email how to join as a member.
first_step.basis: Updates and the newsletter are open to the public, but membership steps are not spelled out on the site.

records.notes: Statewide group with its office at 1501 Cherry Street, Philadelphia (listed as the new mailing address). The site reports a leadership change with an interim director, with no date given; no names are recorded. The membership fee amount is not stated; a member testimonial mentions an annual fee. The volunteer page lists committee and board seats, with no sign-up steps or time commitment. The upcoming events page lists no events.

records.name: Pennsylvania Health Access Network
records.summary: A statewide group that helps people get and keep health coverage. Its helpline offers free help with applying, enrolling, and sorting out coverage problems, and it runs campaigns to protect Medicaid and affordable care.
records.what_you_do: Call or text the helpline for free coverage help, share your story for advocacy work, or join the mailing list to volunteer with enrollment help and advocacy campaigns.

schedule.text: The helpline takes calls and texts, but its hours are not stated on the site. Press statements and advocacy actions are posted as they happen.

cost.text: Free help with health coverage, according to the site.

first_step.how: Call or text the helpline at (877) 570-3642 for free help with your health coverage.
first_step.basis: The helpline is aimed at people who need help understanding and enrolling in coverage, and a phone call or text is the clear first step.

records.notes: Lead was the Pennsylvania Health Access Network home page. The group is statewide with its office address in Philadelphia. Helpline hours are not stated. Dated items with a year: an October 08, 2026 poll statement, a July 30, 2026 statement and a July 23, 2026 statement. The free_help_clinics interest is the closest tag for free enrollment help.

records.name: Keystone Energy Efficiency Alliance
records.notes: Hidden as out of scope. The site describes membership, a member list and a member payment portal, so it appears to be a membership group for energy efficiency businesses and contractors, alongside policy work and a newsletter. Member types are not stated. Dated items with a year: December 17, 2025 (board announcement), November 5, 2025 and October 8, 2025 news posts. The upcoming events page lists only Energy Efficiency Alliance webinars and trainings, with no year and no KEEA events. The owner may choose to publish it as a policy or advocacy group if they consider it in scope.

records.name: Action Reconciliation Service for Peace
records.notes: The lead URL actionreconciliation.org redirects to us.asf-ev.de, the US program of Aktion Sühnezeichen Friedensdienste (based in Berlin). Its volunteer service is based in Camden, New Jersey, and its only Philadelphia link is one volunteer placement at Cradles to Crayons Philadelphia. Marked out_of_area; a reviewer can reclassify if Philadelphia placements are regular. The page read does not mention Quakers, so the Quaker link comes from the lead note only. Latest dated item: an August 29, 2025 anniversary event in Camden.

leads_only.name: Cradles to Crayons Philadelphia
leads_only.note: Named on the Action Reconciliation Service for Peace page as the Philadelphia host of one of its volunteer placements. Link not captured, not checked.

notes: The input file is labelled congregations and faith community programs, but all 8 leads are partner groups from the Friends Center tenant directory (wave w13-congregations, agent r-quaker-meetings). None is a congregation or faith community, so no faith audience was set. Every lead had its own website and all 8 were fetched. Verdicts: 6 publish, 1 hide (Keystone Energy Efficiency Alliance, out_of_scope, owner may reverse), 1 out_of_area (Action Reconciliation Service for Peace). The ACE Mentor Program of America lead was resolved to its Greater Philadelphia affiliate (own site acementorphilly.org, found with the single search), so the national lead has no separate record. Dates are used only when a year is written on the page: the Physicians for Social Responsibility blog posts (month and day only) and the PYSC calendar (no year) are not used as dated evidence. The Housing Alliance site reports an executive director transition with no date; no names recorded. No pages were blocked and no rate limiting was seen. WebSearch budget: 1 of 1 used. WebFetch: 34 used of 60.
